_comment: Story arcs -- a thread. An arc is one goal_flag reached by any of several ROUTES, so a looker, a reasoner and a maker arrive at the same understanding by different means. A route's unlock_when uses the same clause grammar as everything else (OR of ANDs). The ROUTES are authoring apparatus: nothing in play reads them, they are checked at boot and findings go to wayworn-hush.log, so a renamed flag or a deleted encounter that strands a route is caught here rather than in play. An arc with fewer than two routes is reported UNLESS it has a `line` -- an errand someone asked of him may honestly have one way to discharge it. `line` is what he writes in his agenda (omit it and the arc stays invisible scaffolding); `known_when` is when he learns it; `window` is the hours and days the world will receive it, in the same clause grammar (`between`, `day_min`, `day_max`). A shut window never FAILS a thread -- it only says 'not now'. See docs/design/MAP-ARCHITECTURE.md section 6.

arcs.line: Clear the storm debris from Mr. Richards' trail.
